sections.title: Ask how recommendations are proved
sections.body: Ask shortlisted providers to connect observations to actions, affected URLs, owners and checks. A report should distinguish what was seen from what was inferred. This makes it possible to challenge priorities without discarding useful research.

sections.title: Test the provider with a bounded brief
sections.body: Give each provider the same small scenario. Compare the questions they ask, assumptions they expose, exclusions they state and format they propose. A sales promise is less useful than seeing the normal handoff your team would receive.

sections.title: Review access and confidentiality controls
sections.body: Confirm what access is necessary, where credentials remain, who can see client information and how access closes. Proportionate access reduces risk and shows whether the provider understands agency boundaries.

sections.title: Check client-facing white-label controls
sections.body: Review report branding, file names, document properties, links, notifications, meetings and author labels. Agree whether delivery is agency-only or client-facing, and who may communicate outside the approved route.

sections.title: Find the real delivery and review owners
sections.body: Ask who performs the work, who checks it, how questions escalate and what happens when capacity changes. Continuity matters because agency teams need a reliable route for context, challenge and approval.

sections.title: Choose the provider your workflow can absorb
sections.body: The best fit reduces decision load. It gives account leads a clear summary, writers useful briefs, developers assignable tickets and reviewers enough evidence. A technically strong provider can still be a poor fit if every handoff needs reconstruction.
